title: Female reproductive system anatomy
description: A cyclic system: ovulation, fertilisation in the tube, implantation in the endometrium.

questions.question: What organs are included in the female reproductive system?
questions.answer: The system includes ovaries, uterine tubes, uterus, cervix, vagina and external genital structures. Each has distinct roles in cycles, reproduction and pelvic support.

questions.question: Where does fertilization usually occur?
questions.answer: Fertilization most often occurs in the ampulla of a uterine tube. The resulting early embryo travels toward the uterine cavity.

questions.question: What is the fundus & body?
questions.answer: The domed fundus above the tubal openings and the tapering body, of smooth muscle (myometrium) lined by endometrium. Function: Houses and nourishes a pregnancy; the myometrium generates labour.

questions.question: Where is the cervix located?
questions.answer: The fibrous neck projecting into the vagina, with an endocervical canal of mucus-secreting columnar epithelium and a squamous ectocervix. Function: Keeps pregnancy in and microbes out; dilates 10 cm in labour.

questions.question: What is the function of the uterine tube?
questions.answer: Function: Captures the oocyte, is the site of fertilisation (ampulla) and transports the embryo by ciliary beat and peristalsis. A 10 cm ciliated duct with interstitial, isthmic, ampullary and infundibular parts.
